title: We spent 9 months making Necromancer: Ash & Bone using AI for code, art, and audio. Here's how it went.
author: EPGHypheN
selftext:
Hey everyone! I'm part of the [Binx.TV](http://Binx.TV) team, and we recently released **Necromancer: Ash & Bone** on Steam Early Access.  
  
We spent 9 months developing the game, using AI for code, graphics, and audio throughout the process.  
  
It started with us explaining an idea and going back and forth until playing as a necromancer felt right. The first thing we worked on was bringing defeated enemies back to life. Once that worked, we started brainstorming every skill, artifact, and enemy we could add.  
  
We eventually shipped when we thought the game was decent and fun enough. Then came the community feedback, and some of it was pretty harsh haha. Players said the sprites felt disconnected, the sounds were horrible, and the gameplay was too basic.  
  
So we put more effort into the design and overall feel of the game. We followed a LOT of community suggestions, but we also said no to some.  
  
For example, several players wanted an extra action button, like a dash for repositioning in tight situations. We decided against it because that was an intentional part of how we wanted the game to play.  
  
AI helped us build the game throughout those 9 months, but deciding what worked and what didn't still came down to our own judgment and the feedback we received.  
  
Anyway, here's [Necromancer: Ash & Bone on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4883600/Necromancer_Ash__Bone/) if you want to see how it turned out!  
  
Feel free to join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/nw9FZnG25R) as well if you'd like to follow updates or hang out with the community.
